  next: assignCustomerCode

save:

  next: respond

respond:

OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
            E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; a leading '+' and
            country code are kept, otherwise '+61' is assumed and a single leading
            '0' is dropped from the national digits. The result must carry 8 to 15
            digits after the '+'. The normalized E.164 value is stored and returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be a
            syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            When omitted on create it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Create-time hint that this owner deliberately shares a household with an
            existing owner. When true, the duplicate-household check (same lastName and
            same address, compared case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace) is
            bypassed so the owner can be created despite the collision. Not persisted.
          type: boolean
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.

## What I did

Following the OfficeFloor function-injection pattern already used for email/telephone normalization, I introduced **address normalization on owner creation**.

**New files**
- `NormalizeOwnerAddress.java` — a pipeline step that mutates the validated request's address in place: trims and collapses whitespace, upper-cases, and expands abbreviations (`ST→STREET`, `RD→ROAD`, `AVE→AVENUE`) token-by-token. It holds the static `normalize(String)` that is the single source of truth for "normalized address." If the address is **blank after normalization**, it throws `InvalidAddressException` (the required-field check now runs against the normalized form).
- `InvalidAddressException.java` + `InvalidAddressExceptionHandler.java` — checked exception mapping to **400**, mirroring the existing `InvalidTelephoneException` machinery.
- `escalation/…InvalidAddressException.yml` — wires the handler.

**Edits**
- `owners.POST.yml` — inserted the `normalizeAddress` step after `normalizeEmail`, so the address is normalized *before* the household duplicate check and before the entity is built/stored/returned.
- `CheckOwnerHouseholdUnique.sameHousehold` — address comparison now goes through `NormalizeOwnerAddress.normalize` (so case/whitespace/abbreviation differences never split a household, including against un-normalized seed data).
- `AssignOwnerHousehold` — the shared `householdId` derivation now uses the normalized address too, keeping the 409 bypass and the id assignment consistent.

## How it satisfies the spec
- **Store/return normalized address**: the request is mutated in place, so `BuildOwner` maps the normalized value into the persisted entity (verified by the two acceptance tests: `"  12  main  st "` → `"12 MAIN STREET"`, `"7 elm ave"` → `"7 ELM AVENUE"`).
- **Required-field check rejects blank-after-normalization**: `"   "` passes the raw `minLength:1` but normalizes to empty, so `InvalidAddressException` → 400 (verified).
- **All address comparisons use the normalized form**: both household duplicate detection and the shared household id route through `NormalizeOwnerAddress.normalize`.
